segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Sit comfortably and soften the muscles around the eyes. Let attention approach the space between the eyebrows without strain.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Imagine a small violet compass resting behind the brow. It does not predict the future; it simply gives attention a place to return.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel one inhale and exhale while the compass needle settles. Keep the gaze soft behind closed eyelids.
[soft, slow, warm voice] When thought pulls north, south, yesterday, or tomorrow, notice the journey and return to the centre point.
[soft, slow, warm voice] No colour or sensation is required. The compass can be imagined, faint, or absent while attention remains gentle.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Broaden briefly to the whole forehead, temples, and face. Release any pressure before returning to the small point.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Rest with centre and spaciousness together... one quiet needle floating inside a much wider sky.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If an image appears, let it change. If darkness remains, let darkness be complete enough.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Continue the simple cycle: wandering... noticing... returning to the violet coordinate.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Clarity may come or not come. The practice is attention, not a promise of special perception.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the compass grow transparent. Include breath, chest, hands, and the contact points beneath you.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Hear sounds in the room while keeping a faint sense of the brow. Inner and outer coordinates can coexist.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Move your hands, open your eyes, and let the compass become an ordinary memory.
